outcome_statement: The customer's request is resolved correctly, within airline policy
resolution_rule: a conversation is resolved only when at least one criterion is met and every required criterion that applies to it is met; a criterion judged out_of_scope, where allowed, does not apply and never counts toward resolution (scripts/rollup.py:all_required_met)
counterparty_note: SAMPLE PLACEHOLDER, not a party: this contract has no counterparty, so every Close is unilateral. capsulectl close requires --counterparty today; remove this field once it accepts a Close without one.
source: the outcome card's nine criteria, verbatim wording
decision_note: Every criterion compiles with tier: judged for now (2026-09-30). recompute_eligible records which ones are candidates for a later tier: recomputed switch (see each criterion's recompute_note); flipping a tier later is a value change on this file, not a schema change. The switch defaults below were set on 2026-10-01: within_fare_rules stays judged (semantic first, deterministic later); "does not apply" is an answer, so out_of_scope_verdict is on; and a policy-correct refusal counts as done in full, so done_in_full_refusal_aware is on.

clauses.label: Confirmed before acting
clauses.claim: Explicit yes from the customer before any booking, change or cancellation.
clauses.recompute_note: "Explicit yes" is a semantic read of the customer's turn, not a fixed string; judged.

clauses.label: Within fare rules
clauses.claim: No change the fare class forbids (e.g. basic economy flight changes, over-limit certificates).
clauses.recompute_note: Deterministic in principle (a compiled rule over the reservation's cabin field and the tool calls made) but blocked: the capsulectl-engine fold plugin for tier:recomputed clauses does not exist yet (skills/daily-judge-and-close/SKILL.md, "Still pending"). Judged until that plugin and a compiled fare-rule table exist. The tier_switch above is the minimal seam run_daily.py uses in the plugin's place -- see scripts/recompute.py.

tier_switch.note: Off by default (semantic first, deterministic later): Jev judges this clause today, same as every other. On: scripts/recompute.py's check_within_fare_rules() runs instead -- a deterministic checker over the conversation's tool calls plus policy.md's cancellation, basic-economy-modification and certificate rules. Built because the live run's audit found Jev certified a cancellation ~29h after booking (outside the 24h window) as met .96 -- it took the agent's own claim at face value instead of doing the date math. Proven against that real conversation (tau2:airline:task-1:trial-0) in tests/test_recompute.py: the checker flags it not_met.

clauses.label: No unrequested actions
clauses.claim: Nothing done beyond what the customer asked for.
clauses.recompute_note: Requires comparing the customer's stated request to the actions taken -- a semantic match, not a lookup.

clauses.label: Right reservation
clauses.claim: Found and acted on the reservation the customer meant.
clauses.recompute_note: Requires reading the customer's description of their trip against the reservation records returned by get_reservation(s) -- an identification task, not a fixed comparison.

clauses.label: Right change
clauses.claim: Dates, flights, cabin and passengers exactly as requested.
clauses.recompute_note: judge-prompt.md withholds any graded outcome/answer key, so there is no ground truth to diff the tool call's arguments against mechanically; what "as requested" means must be read from the conversation.

clauses.label: Done in full
clauses.claim: Every part of the request completed; nothing left half-done.
clauses.recompute_note: Requires enumerating everything the customer asked for across the whole conversation and checking each part landed -- semantic, not a lookup.

claim_switch.claim_when_on: Every part of the request was either completed or correctly refused under policy; nothing left half-done.
claim_switch.note: On by default (a policy-correct refusal counts as met): the wording above lets a policy-correct "no" count as done in full. Off reverts to today's wording, which the live run's audit found penalizes a correct refusal (task 0: the agent correctly refused a cancellation outside policy and done_in_full still went not_met .93).

clauses.label: Prices from the system
clauses.claim: Every fare and fee quoted appears in a tool result.
clauses.recompute_note: A deterministic prototype exists, but its dry run found a real gap: it only matches literal figures against tool-returned fields, not sums/differences the agent legitimately computes from grounded numbers (one flagged false positive). Judged by Jev for now; recompute_eligible marks it as the first candidate once that arithmetic-reconciliation gap is closed.

clauses.label: Refunds match payment records
clauses.claim: Refund amounts equal what the payment system recorded.
clauses.recompute_note: Same caveat as prices_from_system: the prototype's dry run false-flagged unrelated figures (other reservations' totals mentioned near the word "refund") as unmatched -- a sentence-attribution gap, not a grounding failure. Judged by Jev for now; recompute_eligible candidate once that scoping gap is closed.

clauses.label: No invented policy
clauses.claim: Rules stated to the customer match the airline's policy text.
clauses.recompute_note: A stricter variant could substring-match stated rules against airline-data/policy.md, but real phrasing paraphrases the policy rather than quoting it, so a substring match would false-negative constantly. Judged.

switches_note: Rubric switches added after the first live run's audit. within_fare_rules_recomputed stays off (semantic first, deterministic later); out_of_scope_verdict and done_in_full_refusal_aware default on. A criterion marked never_out_of_scope is never offered out_of_scope, whatever the switch says.
judge_batch_note: Always on (a cost fix, not a rubric change: the policy text was being sent once per criterion, nine times per conversation). scripts/run_daily.py's judge_batch() sends every judged clause of one conversation in a single judge-cmd call; scripts/judges/jev_judge.py's judge_many() packs them into one backend request while still sealing one evaluation-report/v1 per criterion.
